meaning: casual sentence-ender used to confirm or recall something half-forgotten (was it...? / what was...again?)

exercises.example_sentence: 来週の会議は、確か水曜日だっけ？
exercises.translation: Next week's meeting is on Wednesday, right? (I can't quite remember.)
wrong_choice_explanations: なの asks the listener for information ('is it Wednesday?'). 確か水曜日なの？ would be requesting the date from someone else, but 確か shows the speaker half-remembers it themselves and is checking their own memory — the recall that だっけ expresses.

だね invites light agreement with an on-the-spot judgement ('it's Wednesday, isn't it'). 確か水曜日だね？ treats the date as something both parties can see is so, not something the speaker is struggling to recall; the recall sense belongs to だっけ.

だけ means 'only.' 確か水曜日だけ？ would ask whether the meeting is only on Wednesday, a question about how many days it runs, not about whether the speaker has remembered the day correctly; だっけ marks that act of recall.
exercises.hiragana_full: らいしゅうのかいぎは、たしかすいようびだっけ？

audio_alternatives.kanji: 確認だけど、今度の会議って水曜日だっけ？
audio_alternatives.hiragana_full: かくにんだけど、こんどのかいぎってすいようびだっけ？

audio_alternatives.kanji: 来週の会議は水曜日でしたよね？
audio_alternatives.hiragana_full: らいしゅうのかいぎはすいようびでしたよね？

exercises.example_sentence: あの有名な俳優、名前は何て言ったっけ？
exercises.translation: That famous actor — what was his name again?
wrong_choice_explanations: たの asks the listener for information ('what did he say?'). 名前は何て言ったの？ would be asking someone else what the actor said, whereas the speaker is trying to recall a name they once knew — the self-directed 'what was it again?' of っけ.
たよ asserts a fact to the listener ('he said…!'). 何て言ったよ？ is contradictory — a statement ending combined with a question word — and can't express the speaker searching their own memory, which っけ does.

ただろう conjectures about the past ('he probably said'). 何て言っただろう？ would be the speaker guessing or asking the listener to guess, not reaching for a name they knew and have temporarily lost; that recall is what っけ marks.
exercises.hiragana_full: あのゆうめいなはいゆう、なまえはなんていったっけ？

audio_alternatives.kanji: ほら、あの有名な俳優、名前なんだっけ？
audio_alternatives.hiragana_full: ほら、あのゆうめいなはいゆう、なまえなんだっけ？

audio_alternatives.kanji: あの有名な俳優の名前が、どうしても思い出せない。
audio_alternatives.hiragana_full: あのゆうめいなはいゆうのなまえが、どうしてもおもいだせない。

exercises.example_sentence: あれ、この部屋の鍵、どこに置いたっけ？
exercises.translation: Huh, where did I put the key to this room again?
wrong_choice_explanations: たの asks the listener about a fact ('where did you put it?'). どこに置いたの？ would be directed at someone else, but with あれ the speaker is questioning their own memory of where they put the key — っけ.

たよね seeks confirmation of something the speaker is fairly sure of ('I put it…, didn't I?'). どこに置いたよね？ makes no sense with a question word, since there's no claim to confirm; the speaker has drawn a blank, which っけ expresses.

ただろう guesses about a past action ('I probably put it…'). どこに置いただろう？ would be idle speculation, whereas the speaker is trying to retrieve where they actually put the key — the memory-search sense of っけ.
exercises.hiragana_full: あれ、このへやのかぎ、どこにおいたっけ？

audio_alternatives.kanji: この部屋の鍵、私どこに置いたっけ？
audio_alternatives.hiragana_full: このへやのかぎ、わたしどこにおいたっけ？

audio_alternatives.kanji: あれ、部屋の鍵をどこに置いたか思い出せない。
audio_alternatives.hiragana_full: あれ、へやのかぎをどこにおいたかおもいだせない。

exercises.example_sentence: その映画、私たちもう見たっけ？
exercises.translation: That movie — have we already seen it? (I forget.)
wrong_choice_explanations: たよね seeks agreement with something the speaker believes ('we saw it, didn't we?'). もう見たよね？ presumes we did see it, but the speaker can't remember whether we did at all; っけ marks that genuine blank.

たの asks the listener for information ('did you see it?'). 私たちもう見たの？ is odd with 私たち as subject — the speaker would be asking the listener about their own shared experience — whereas っけ marks the speaker trying to recall it themselves.

ただろう conjectures ('we probably saw it'). もう見ただろう？ would be the speaker guessing or pressing the listener to agree, not searching their memory for whether they had seen the film — the recall sense that っけ carries.
exercises.hiragana_full: そのえいが、わたしたちもうみたっけ？

audio_alternatives.kanji: ねえ、この映画ってもう見たっけ？
audio_alternatives.hiragana_full: ねえ、このえいがってもうみたっけ？

audio_alternatives.kanji: その映画、私たちもう見ましたよね？
audio_alternatives.hiragana_full: そのえいが、わたしたちもうみましたよね？

exercises.example_sentence: あれ、このケーキ、前はこんなに甘かったっけ？
exercises.translation: Huh, was this cake always this sweet?
wrong_choice_explanations: かったよね seeks agreement with a belief ('it was sweet, right?'). 前はこんなに甘かったよね？ presumes the speaker remembers it being this sweet, but the surprised あれ shows they can't match the present taste to their memory; かったっけ marks that uncertainty.

かったね shares a judgement for light agreement ('that was sweet, wasn't it'). 前はこんなに甘かったね？ treats the past sweetness as a settled shared fact, whereas the speaker is questioning their own memory of it — the job of っけ.

かっただろう guesses about the past ('it was probably sweet'). 前はこんなに甘かっただろう？ would be the speaker speculating or urging the listener to agree, not trying to recall whether the cake used to taste like this — っけ.
exercises.hiragana_full: あれ、このけーき、まえはこんなにあまかったっけ？

audio_alternatives.kanji: このケーキ、こんなに甘かったっけ？
audio_alternatives.hiragana_full: このけーき、こんなにあまかったっけ？

audio_alternatives.kanji: 前に食べたとき、このケーキはこんなに甘くなかった気がする。
audio_alternatives.hiragana_full: まえにたべたとき、このけーきはこんなにあまくなかったきがする。

exercises.example_sentence: 君の誕生日って、確か五月だっけ？
exercises.translation: Your birthday is in May, isn't it? (If I recall correctly.)
wrong_choice_explanations: なの asks the listener directly ('is it May?'). 確か五月なの？ would simply request the information, but 確か shows the speaker already half-remembers and is checking a hazy memory against the listener — what だっけ does.

だね invites agreement with an on-the-spot observation ('it's May, isn't it'). 確か五月だね？ treats the birthday as obvious to both parties rather than something the speaker is trying to recall, which is what だっけ expresses.

だったら means 'if it is…' and opens a conditional clause. 確か五月だったら？ is a dangling fragment ('if it's May, then…?') with no main clause, and it says nothing about trying to remember; だっけ turns the half-recalled month into a confirmation question.
exercises.hiragana_full: きみのたんじょうびって、たしかごがつだっけ？

audio_alternatives.kanji: 確か君の誕生日って五月だっけ？
audio_alternatives.hiragana_full: たしかきみのたんじょうびってごがつだっけ？

audio_alternatives.kanji: あなたの誕生日は五月でしたよね？
audio_alternatives.hiragana_full: あなたのたんじょうびはごがつでしたよね？

exercises.example_sentence: あれ、朝の薬、もう飲んだっけ？
exercises.translation: Hmm, did I already take my morning medicine?
wrong_choice_explanations: だよね seeks agreement with a belief ('I took it, right?'). もう飲んだよね？ presumes the speaker took the medicine, but あれ shows they can't remember whether they did at all; だっけ marks that blank in memory.

だね invites light agreement with a shared observation ('I took it, didn't I'). もう飲んだね？ treats having taken the medicine as evident, but the point is that the speaker can't recall doing so — what だっけ expresses.
だろう expresses conjecture ('I probably took it'). もう飲んだろう？ would be a guess, not an attempt to retrieve the memory of actually taking the medicine; だっけ is the self-questioning ending for that.
exercises.hiragana_full: あれ、あさのくすり、もうのんだっけ？

audio_alternatives.kanji: あれ、私もう薬飲んだっけ？
audio_alternatives.hiragana_full: あれ、わたしもうくすりのんだっけ？

audio_alternatives.kanji: 朝の薬を飲んだかどうか、思い出せない。
audio_alternatives.hiragana_full: あさのくすりをのんだかどうか、おもいだせない。

exercises.example_sentence: 明日の待ち合わせは、駅前だっけ？
exercises.translation: Tomorrow's meeting spot is in front of the station, right? (I forget.)
wrong_choice_explanations: だけ means 'only.' 駅前だけ？ would ask whether the station front is the only meeting place, a question about alternatives, not about whether the speaker has remembered the arrangement; だっけ marks that memory check.

だね invites agreement with an on-the-spot judgement ('it's the station, isn't it'). 駅前だね？ treats the meeting place as evident to both rather than something the speaker is trying to recall, which is what だっけ marks.

なの asks the listener for information ('is it in front of the station?'). 駅前なの？ would be a plain request for the place, but the translation's 'I forget' shows the speaker once knew it and is dredging it up — the recall sense of だっけ.
exercises.hiragana_full: あしたのまちあわせは、えきまえだっけ？

audio_alternatives.kanji: 明日の集合場所って、駅前だっけ？
audio_alternatives.hiragana_full: あしたのしゅうごうばしょって、えきまえだっけ？

audio_alternatives.kanji: 明日の待ち合わせは駅前でしたよね？
audio_alternatives.hiragana_full: あしたのまちあわせはえきまえでしたよね？

exercises.example_sentence: 家を出るとき、ちゃんと鍵をかけたっけ？
exercises.translation: When I left the house, did I actually lock the door?
wrong_choice_explanations: たの asks the listener about a fact ('did you lock it?'). ちゃんと鍵をかけたの？ would be checking on someone else, but the speaker is worrying about their own action as they left — the self-questioning っけ.

たよね seeks confirmation of something the speaker believes ('I locked it, didn't I?'). 鍵をかけたよね？ presumes they did, but the anxiety here is that they can't remember whether they did; っけ marks that uncertainty.

ただろう guesses about a past action ('I probably locked it'). 鍵をかけただろう？ would be speculation or pressing someone to agree, not trying to recall whether the door was actually locked — the recall sense of っけ.
exercises.hiragana_full: いえをでるとき、ちゃんとかぎをかけたっけ？

audio_alternatives.kanji: 出かけるとき、ちゃんと鍵をかけたっけ？
audio_alternatives.hiragana_full: でかけるとき、ちゃんとかぎをかけたっけ？

audio_alternatives.kanji: 家を出るとき鍵をかけたか、心配になってきた。
audio_alternatives.hiragana_full: いえをでるときかぎをかけたか、しんぱいになってきた。

exercises.example_sentence: この人とは、前にどこかで会ったんだっけ？
exercises.translation: This person — have I met them somewhere before? (I can't recall.)
wrong_choice_explanations: んだよ asserts or explains something to the listener ('I did meet them, you see'). 会ったんだよ？ is a statement ending forced into a question and can't express the speaker searching their own memory, which is what んだっけ does.

んだね acknowledges and agrees with what the listener has said ('so we met, I see'). 会ったんだね？ treats the meeting as newly confirmed information, whereas the speaker is trying to recall whether they ever met — んだっけ.
んだろう conjectures ('I suppose we met'). 会ったんだろう？ would be guessing or urging the listener to agree, not retrieving a hazy memory of a past meeting; んだっけ marks that act of recall.
exercises.hiragana_full: このひととは、まえにどこかであったんだっけ？

audio_alternatives.kanji: この人とは、どこかで会ったんだっけ？
audio_alternatives.hiragana_full: このひととは、どこかであったんだっけ？

audio_alternatives.kanji: この人と前に会ったことがある気がするが、思い出せない。
audio_alternatives.hiragana_full: このひととまえにあったことがあるきがするが、おもいだせない。
